executive_summary: This week's coverage centers on a single, well-corroborated story: OpenAI briefed U.S. officials on its unreleased Astra model, which reportedly solved or substantially advanced 10 longstanding problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, while the company simultaneously disclosed it is slowing Astra's development due to concerns it may possess 'critical' cyber capabilities. The story is notable for signaling a rare instance of a frontier lab publicly delaying release over cyber-risk thresholds and for increasing scrutiny on pre-release evaluation processes. Coverage was corroborated across The Information, Semafor, Axios, and AI Magazine. However, the provided story set is narrow and does not capture other likely major developments this week—such as competitor model releases, AI policy/regulatory news, chip/infrastructure updates, or robotics announcements—suggesting this snapshot reflects partial curation rather than a comprehensive view of the week's AI news.

stories.title: OpenAI slows Astra over possible critical cyber capabilities after U.S. briefings
stories.summary: OpenAI told Axios it cannot rule out that its upcoming Astra model has 'critical' cyber capabilities, and is slowing development while expanding safety testing and tightening security controls before release. The company had briefed U.S. officials on Astra's capabilities, and separately claimed an internal version resolved or substantially advanced 10 longstanding problems in mathematics, quantum complexity, and theoretical computer science.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a rare public instance of a frontier lab delaying a model's release over potential cyber-risk thresholds, putting pressure on emerging U.S. pre-release evaluation processes and inviting independent scrutiny of Astra's research claims and safeguards.
